nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is unpaid, the landlord must give written notice stating the rent and late fees owed; the lease terminates if the tenant does not pay within seven business days after receiving it.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice given at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is unpaid, the landlord may give written notice; if the tenant does not pay in full within seven days, the tenancy terminates.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the rental due date named in the notice.

lateFeeCap.detail: The Landlord and Tenant Act does not address late charges; a fee must be agreed to in advance and should reasonably approximate the landlord's actual costs.
lateFeeCap.cite: Alaska Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (AS 34.03) — no late-fee provision

nonpaymentNotice.detail: After written notice of nonpayment, the tenant has five days to pay before the landlord may terminate and file a special detainer action.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice.

lateFeeCap.detail: The statute refers only to a 'reasonable late fee set forth in a written rental agreement'; it sets no dollar or percentage limit.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: A tenant who fails to pay rent when due and does not leave after a three-day written notice to quit commits unlawful detainer.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the termination date named in the notice.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written three-day notice to pay rent or quit; Saturdays, Sundays and judicial holidays are not counted.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord must give 30 days' written notice if the tenant has lived there less than one year and 60 days if one year or more; tenants covered by the Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code § 1946.2) or local ordinances also need just cause.

lateFeeCap.detail: No statute sets a dollar limit, but courts strike late fees that are unreasonable penalties rather than a fair estimate of the landlord's damages.
lateFeeCap.cite: Cal. Civ. Code § 1671; Orozco v. Casimiro (2004) 121 Cal.App.4th Supp. 7

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written 10-day demand to pay rent or give up possession (5 days for certain exempt residential agreements); the notice cannot be waived in the lease.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy of one month up to six months is ended with at least 21 days' written notice (28 days for 6-12 month tenancies, 91 days for 1 year or more); since 2024 most tenants who have lived in a unit 12 months or more cannot be removed without cause.

lateFeeCap.value: Greater of $50 or 5% of past-due rent
lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee can be charged only after rent is at least 7 days late, must be disclosed in the lease, and cannot exceed the greater of $50 or 5% of the past-due rent.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Once rent is unpaid past the 9-day grace period, the landlord may serve a notice to quit giving at least three days before the quit date.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A month-to-month tenancy ends by lapse of time; the notice to quit must give at least three full days and at least until the end of the current rental month. Tenants 62+ or with disabilities in buildings of 5+ units need good cause.

lateFeeCap.value: Lesser of $5/day (max $50) or 5% of the late rent
lateFeeCap.detail: A late charge can be assessed only after the grace period, only once per late payment, and cannot exceed the lesser of $5 per day up to $50 or 5% of the delinquent rent.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: After rent is due, the landlord may give written notice that the lease will end unless the tenant pays within at least 5 days.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month agreement with at least 60 days' written notice, counted from the first day of the month after notice is given.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late charge may not exceed 5% of the monthly rent and cannot be imposed until rent is more than 5 days late.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Before filing for nonpayment, the housing provider must give a written notice of intent to file at least 10 days in advance, and cannot file at all if less than $600 is owed.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: D.C. tenants cannot be evicted, even after a lease or month-to-month term expires, as long as they keep paying rent, except for specific causes listed in the statute.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee may not exceed 5% of the rent due, may be charged only once per late payment after a 5-day grace period, and must be disclosed in the lease.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must deliver a written 3-day notice demanding rent or possession; weekends and court-observed holidays are not counted.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the end of a monthly period.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Before filing a dispossessory affidavit for unpaid rent, the landlord must give a notice to vacate or pay all amounts owed within three business days, posted on the door in a sealed envelope.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord must give a tenant-at-will 60 days' notice to end the tenancy; a tenant must give 30 days.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Since Feb. 5, 2026, the landlord must give a written 10-calendar-day notice to pay; if the tenant schedules state-funded mediation, filing generally must wait until 20 days after notice.
nonpaymentNotice.cite: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 521-68 (as amended by 2025 Act 278)

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord must give at least 45 days' written notice to end a month-to-month tenancy; a tenant must give 28 days.

lateFeeCap.detail: If the rental agreement provides for a late charge, it may not exceed 8% of the rent due.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written 3-day notice demanding the rent due or possession before the tenant is in unlawful detainer.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will (including month-to-month) is ended by written notice of at least one month; landlords must also give 30 days' notice of non-renewal or rent increases.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written demand giving the tenant at least 5 days to pay before ending the lease and filing an eviction.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord ends a month-to-month (or other under-one-year) tenancy with 30 days' written notice.

lateFeeCap.detail: State law sets no dollar limit; the Attorney General says landlords may charge a reasonable late fee. Chicago and suburban Cook County ordinances set their own caps.
lateFeeCap.cite: Ill. Attorney General, Landlord and Tenant Rights

nonpaymentNotice.detail: A landlord may end the lease for unpaid rent with at least 10 days' notice unless the tenant pays in full first or the parties agreed otherwise.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will, including a month-to-month tenancy, is ended by one month's written notice delivered to the tenant.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If the tenant does not pay within three days after written notice of nonpayment, the landlord may end the rental agreement.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date.

lateFeeCap.detail: Late fees are capped based on rent level: $12 per day and $60 per month when rent is $700 or less, and $20 per day and $100 per month when rent is higher.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is unpaid, the landlord may end the agreement if the tenant does not pay within three days (three 24-hour periods) after written notice; two days are added if mailed.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice ending it on a rent-paying date at least 30 days after the notice is received.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Where a city or county has adopted Kentucky's Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, the tenant has 7 days after written notice to pay before the landlord may end the lease; elsewhere no specific statutory pay-or-quit period applies.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: In URLTA localities either party gives 30 days' written notice before a rental date; elsewhere a landlord gives one month's written notice.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must deliver a written notice to vacate giving at least 5 days, but a lease may waive this notice.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A month-to-month lease ends with notice given at least 10 calendar days before the end of the month.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Once rent is at least 7 days late, the landlord may serve a 7-day notice to quit; paying the full amount due before it expires voids the notice.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will must be ended by at least 30 days' written notice from either party.

lateFeeCap.detail: Rent is late only after 15 days, and the penalty may not exceed 4% of one month's rent; the tenant must be told in writing at the start of the tenancy.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Before filing a failure-to-pay-rent case, the landlord must give a written notice of intent to file (on the Judiciary's form) and wait 10 days.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord must give written notice 60 days before the end of a month-to-month tenancy (local laws may differ).

lateFeeCap.detail: A lease cannot impose a late penalty above 5% of the unpaid rent for that period (weekly leases: $3/week, $12/month).

nonpaymentNotice.detail: For unpaid rent, a 14-day written notice to quit ends a lease or tenancy at will; the tenant can generally cure by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, by the answer date.

monthToMonthNotice.value: 30 days or one rental period, whichever is longer
monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will is ended by written notice equal to the interval between rent payments or 30 days, whichever is longer (for monthly rent, a full rental period).

lateFeeCap.value: No late fee until rent is 30 days late
lateFeeCap.detail: A lease may not impose any interest or penalty for late rent until 30 days after the rent was due; the statute sets no specific dollar cap.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written 7-day demand for possession (or 7-day notice to quit) for nonpayment before filing.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a tenancy at will with one month's notice; when rent is paid more often than every 3 months, notice equal to the rental interval is enough.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Before filing for nonpayment, the landlord must give a written notice itemizing the amount owed; the tenant has 14 days (or longer if local law requires) to pay.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will is ended by written notice at least as long as the interval between rent due dates or three months, whichever is less.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee must be agreed to in writing and cannot exceed 8% of the overdue rent payment.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord may give written notice (or email/text if agreed) that the rental agreement will end if rent is not paid within 3 days.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the termination date.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Missouri sets no pay-or-quit period; the landlord must demand the rent and may file a rent-and-possession case once it goes unpaid.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A tenancy at will or for less than a year, including month-to-month, may be ended by one month's written notice to vacate.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If the tenant does not pay within 3 days after written notice of nonpayment, the landlord may end the rental agreement.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with at least 30 days' written notice.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is not paid within 7 calendar days after written notice of nonpayment, the landlord may end the rental agreement.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord serves a written notice to pay rent or surrender by the close of business on the 7th judicial day (court days) after service.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A month-to-month tenant must receive at least 30 days' notice; tenants 60 or older or with disabilities may request extra time.

lateFeeCap.detail: A reasonable late fee may be charged only after rent is at least 3 calendar days late and may not exceed 5% of the periodic rent.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: For unpaid rent, the landlord gives a written demand for rent and a 7-day eviction notice stating the reason and the tenant's right to cure by paying arrears.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Residential tenancies are ended with a 30-day eviction notice, but most rentals ('restricted property') may be ended only for a listed reason, which includes 'other good cause.'

nonpaymentNotice.detail: No notice to quit is required before filing an eviction for nonpayment of rent; other grounds need notices of 3 days to months.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Under the Anti-Eviction Act, a landlord covered by the law cannot evict or refuse to renew a written or oral tenancy without a statutory good cause proved in court.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is not paid within 3 days after written notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate, the owner may end the agreement; paying in full within the 3 days bars the case.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month residency with written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee may not exceed 5% of the rent for each rental period in default, calculated on rent only.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must serve a written rent demand giving at least 14 days to pay or surrender possession before starting a nonpayment case (plus a 5-day late-rent notice by certified mail under RPL § 235-e).

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord ending a tenancy must give 30 days' notice if the tenant has lived there under 1 year, 60 days for 1-2 years, and 90 days for 2+ years; units covered by the Good Cause Eviction Law also need a lawful reason.

lateFeeCap.value: Lesser of $50 or 5% of monthly rent
lateFeeCap.detail: No late fee may be charged until rent is more than 5 days late, and it may not exceed $50 or 5% of the monthly rent, whichever is less.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The lease is forfeited if the tenant fails to pay within 10 days after the landlord demands all past-due rent.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A month-to-month tenancy may be ended with a notice to quit given at least 7 days before the end of the current month (a lease may require more).

lateFeeCap.value: Greater of $15 or 5% of monthly rent
lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee can be charged only once rent is 5 days late, only once per late payment, and cannot exceed $15 or 5% of the monthly rent, whichever is greater.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Once rent is 3 days overdue, the landlord must serve a written 3-day notice of intention to evict before filing.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with at least one calendar month's written notice given at any time, unless they agreed in writing to longer notice.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Before filing an eviction, the landlord must serve a written notice to leave the premises at least three days before filing.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord may end the rental agreement if the tenant does not pay within 5 days after a written demand for rent; the demand also serves as the demand for possession.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the termination date, counted from service.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: For monthly tenancies, the landlord may give a 10-day notice on or after the 8th day of the rental period, or a 13-day notice on or after the 5th day; the notice must state the amount due and the deadline to pay.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: During the first year of occupancy a landlord may end a month-to-month tenancy with 30 days' written notice; after the first year it may end only for tenant cause or a qualifying landlord reason (generally with 90 days' notice and relocation payment).

lateFeeCap.value: Reasonable flat fee, or 5% of rent per 5-day period
lateFeeCap.detail: Late fees require a written agreement and rent unpaid by the 4th day; the fee may be a reasonable flat amount once per period, a daily fee up to 6% of that flat amount, or 5% of the rent for each 5 days late.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: When the tenant fails to pay rent on demand, the notice to quit must give the tenant 10 days to leave (leases may waive this notice).

monthToMonthNotice.detail: For leases of one year or less or of indefinite term (including month-to-month), the notice to quit must give 15 days; leases over one year require 30 days.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Once rent is 15 days in arrears, the landlord must mail a written demand; if the tenant does not pay within 5 days of mailing, the landlord may file (no earlier than the 6th day).

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice delivered at least 30 days before the termination date.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If rent is not paid within 5 days of the due date, the landlord may end the lease after written notice; the notice can be satisfied once per lease term or by conspicuous language in the written lease.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the termination date.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Since 2024 South Dakota no longer requires a 3-day notice to quit; a landlord may file an eviction once rent is unpaid for 3 days after it is due.
nonpaymentNotice.cite: S.D. Codified Laws § 21-16-1(4); § 21-16-2 repealed by 2024 S.D. Sess. Laws ch. 75

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A residential tenancy at will may be ended by the landlord with at least 15 days' notice (two months for active-duty military households, with exceptions).

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must give written notice; the tenant has 14 days after receiving it to pay before the lease ends (the notice may be waived in the lease in bold 12-point type).

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee may be charged only after a 5-day grace period and cannot exceed 10% of the past-due rent.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord must give at least 3 days' written notice to vacate before filing, unless the lease sets a different period; for suits filed since Jan. 1, 2026, a tenant who was not previously late must get a notice to pay rent or vacate.
nonpaymentNotice.cite: Tex. Prop. Code § 24.005(a) (as amended by SB 38, 2025)

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy; it ends on the later of the date in the notice or one month after notice is given, unless the parties agreed otherwise in writing.

lateFeeCap.detail: A late fee requires notice in the written lease and can be charged once rent is unpaid two full days after it was due; it is presumed reasonable if no more than 12% of monthly rent in buildings with up to four units or 10% in larger buildings (higher only if it reflects actual damages).

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord serves a written notice to pay rent and other amounts due or surrender the premises; the tenant has three business days to comply.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: For a month-to-month tenancy, the landlord must serve a notice to quit at least 15 calendar days before the end of the rental period.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: The landlord may end a tenancy for nonpayment with actual notice of a termination date at least 14 days away; paying all rent due through the end of the rental period before then stops the termination.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Without a written lease, a no-cause termination of a monthly tenancy needs at least 60 days' notice if the tenant has lived there 2 years or less and 90 days if longer.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: If the tenant does not pay within 14 days after written notice of nonpayment and intent to terminate, the landlord may end the rental agreement and seek possession.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: Either party may end a month-to-month tenancy with written notice at least 30 days before the next rent due date, unless the rental agreement sets a different period.

lateFeeCap.value: Lesser of 10% of periodic rent or 10% of remaining balance
lateFeeCap.detail: A late charge must be in the written lease and cannot exceed the lesser of 10% of the periodic rent or 10% of the remaining balance owed.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: Residential landlords must serve a 14-day notice to pay rent or vacate before filing an unlawful detainer.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A landlord may not end a month-to-month or other periodic tenancy except for causes listed in the statute (such as nonpayment, owner move-in, or sale).

lateFeeCap.value: No statutory cap (none within 5 days of due date)
lateFeeCap.detail: Washington sets no dollar or percentage limit, but a landlord may not charge a late fee on rent paid within 5 days after it is due; in eviction cases tenants can reinstate by paying late fees only up to $75 total.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: West Virginia does not require a written notice before a landlord files a petition to evict for unpaid rent; the tenant can still pay all rent, interest and costs before trial to end the case.

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A periodic tenancy of less than a year may be ended by notice for one full period before the end of a period.

nonpaymentNotice.detail: For month-to-month tenants and leases of one year or less, the landlord may give a 5-day notice to pay rent or vacate (or a 14-day notice to vacate in some cases).

monthToMonthNotice.detail: A periodic tenancy is ended by written notice of at least 28 days (shorter only for tenancies paid more often than monthly).

nonpaymentNotice.detail: After rent is 3 days late, the landlord must serve a written notice to quit at least 3 days before filing a forcible entry and detainer action.
